title: Two determinant bounds for low formal derivatives
statement:
Let $L$ be a characteristic-zero field, $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in A$ have respective finite orders $d_i\ge0$. Choose pairwise incomparable vertices $a_i\in\mathbf N^d$ with $|a_i|=d_i$, ordered by nondecreasing degree, and set $D=\bigcup_i(a_i+\mathbf N^d)$ and $\Delta_i=\{\beta:a_i+\beta\notin\bigcup_{j<i}(a_j+\mathbf N^d)\}$. For $t\ge0$, let $B_t$ have rows $|\gamma|\le t$ and columns $Y^\beta f_i(X+Y)\bmod(Y)^{t+1}$, $|\beta|\le t$, and let $B'_t$ restrict to $\beta\in\Delta_i$. Suppose these matrices have the same column span, their constant matrices have rank $r_t=\#\{\gamma\in D:|\gamma|\le t\}$, exactly $r_t$ columns of $B'_t$ satisfy $|\beta|+d_i\le t$, and the square submatrix $C_t$ on these columns and the rows $D\cap\{|\gamma|\le t\}$ has unit determinant. Put $J_t$ equal to the ideal of $(r_t+1)$-minors of $B_t$ [def-trf-minor-ideal], and $E=(\partial^\nu f_i:|\nu|<d_i)$ [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Then the $(r_t+1)$-minors of $B'_t$ generate $J_t$, and
$$J_t\subseteq E\quad\text{for every }t\ge0.$$
For every $i$, $0\le t<d_i$ and $\gamma\notin D$ with $|\gamma|\le t$, one also has
$$\partial^\gamma f_i\in J_t+(\partial^\alpha f_i:\alpha\in D,\ |\alpha|\le t).$$
These assertions hold with the empty determinant equal to $1$ and with oversized minors generating the zero ideal; no Jacobian or later-block derivative hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $b_{\gamma,i eta}$ for the entries of either Taylor matrix. Specialize [lem-trf-formal-transverse-shift-calculus] to $m=r=d$, no $T$ variables, $W=X$, $\phi(W)=W$, and the single series $f_i$ depending only on its old $Y$ variables. The hypothesis $\phi\in(W)L[[W]]^d$ holds. Its coefficient formula, with the new variables renamed $Y$, gives $[Y^
u]f_i(X+Y)=\partial^
u f_i(X)/
u!$, where $
u!=\prod_j
u_j!$. Multiplication by $Y^ eta$ therefore gives $b_{\gamma,i eta}=0$ if $ eta
leq\gamma$, and $b_{\gamma,i eta}=\partial^{\gamma- eta}f_i/(\gamma- eta)!$ otherwise. Truncating does not change these entries for $|\gamma|\le t$. All these factorials are units because $L$ is a characteristic-zero field.

source.place: Formal coefficient calculation specialized from lem-trf-formal-transverse-shift-calculus; Tag 0306 is power-series notation only, not a source for the Taylor formula.

proof.text: Fix $t$ and put $k=r_t+1$. Since the two finite matrices have the same column span over $A$, choose column coefficients $H$ with $B_t=B'_tH$. For any $k$ chosen rows $I$ and columns $T$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] to $B'_t[I,:]H[:,T]$. Its determinant is a finite $A$-linear combination of $k$-minors of $B'_t$. Thus $J_k(B_t)\subseteq J_k(B'_t)$ by [def-trf-minor-ideal]. Conversely every column of $B'_t$ is a selected column of $B_t$, so each of its minors is a minor of $B_t$, with the inherited ordering. Hence $J_k(B'_t)=J_k(B_t)=J_t$. Cauchy--Binet also covers fewer than $k$ columns by its empty-sum convention; if there are fewer than $k$ rows there are no such minors.

Call the $r_t$ columns of $B'_t$ with $|\beta|+d_i\le t$ good. Every other column has $|\beta|+d_i>t$. For any row $|\gamma|\le t$ with $\beta\le\gamma$, its entry from step 1 has derivative order $|\gamma-\beta|=|\gamma|-|\beta|\le t-|\beta|<d_i$, hence belongs to $E$; the other entries are zero. Any selection of $r_t+1$ columns contains a column that is not good, since exactly $r_t$ are good. Expand the selected square determinant along that column, using [lem-trf-minor-laplace-coefficient-formula] with $s=1$. Every summand is an entry in $E$ times a signed complementary determinant, so the determinant belongs to $E$. Together with step 2 this proves $J_t\subseteq E$. Oversized minors generate zero by [def-trf-minor-ideal].

source.place: Tag 07Z7 (lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors), row/column-expansion hint; explicit Taylor-column argument supplied by Q11.

proof.text: Fix $i$, $t<d_i$ and $\gamma\notin D$, $|\gamma|\le t$. In $B_t$ select the good columns and the extra column $(i,0)$, and the pivot rows $R_t=D\cap\{|\alpha|\le t\}$ and extra row $\gamma$, retaining their original orders. These are distinct selections: $(i,0)$ is not good since $d_i>t$, and $\gamma\notin R_t$. The resulting $(r_t+1)$-minor has determinant in $J_t$ by [def-trf-minor-ideal]. Expand along $(i,0)$ by [lem-trf-minor-laplace-coefficient-formula] with $s=1$. The term at row $\gamma$ is $\varepsilon\det(C_t)\partial^\gamma f_i/\gamma!$, with $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$; every other term is an $A$-multiple of $\partial^\alpha f_i/\alpha!$ for some $\alpha\in R_t$, by step 1. The coefficient $\varepsilon\det(C_t)/\gamma!$ is a unit, so solving this equality gives precisely $\partial^\gamma f_i\in J_t+(\partial^\alpha f_i:\alpha\in D,|\alpha|\le t)$. For $r_t=0$ this is the $1\times1$ expansion with complementary determinant $1$. If no such $i,t,\gamma$ exists the assertion is vacuous.

Only proof, proof_deps, proof_origin, searches, split_report and status changed; statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are identical to live, which is still unsplit, so nothing is superseded. There is no repair note and no cycle. Step 1: the shift calculus with m=r=d, no T variables, phi=W and f_i(Y) gives the entries b = d^{gamma-beta} f_i/(gamma-beta)!, and the factorials are units in characteristic 0. Step 2: B_t = B'_t H, and Cauchy-Binet applied to the k x n' times n' x k product gives J(B_t) inside J(B'_t); the reverse holds because B'_t is a column restriction. Fitting (3) does not apply here because it needs a square C. Step 3: in a column with |beta|+d_i>t the entries have derivative order below d_i, so they lie in E. Exactly r_t columns are good, so any r_t+1 columns include a bad one; Laplace with s=1 along it gives J_t in E. If d_i=0 there are no bad columns from i. Step 4: border the good columns with column (i,0), which is not good since d_i>t, and the rows R_t with row gamma. The cofactor at gamma is ±det C_t, a unit, which gives the second bound. Small cases checked: X^2 with t=0,1,2, XY with t=1, and the empty and r_t=0 cases. Stacks tags 07Z7 and 0F0K match the tag table. The Cauchy-Binet tool use from sk-thm-p1 is accepted; its other cited nodes are in unit sk-i-curve-zero. No SGA citations.
